Robert Lempert is a researcher at RAND who works to help communities understand and manage climate risks. He also has a personal connection to disaster, losing his home in the 2025 L.A. fires.

Hear about his experience in this @latimes interview: piped.video/watch?v=URRwHM3v…
Jacob Parakilas of @RANDEurope discusses how Ukraine uses military ground robotics for critical support on the battlefield. bit.ly/4cVD9RU
New paper outlines a research agenda for understanding AI's impact on chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risk. bit.ly/48bErWj

Could deep sea mining break China's grip on critical minerals?

Here's what our research says about the challenges facing Washington: bit.ly/4tYcp9d

China has emerged as America's primary pacing threat.

This new report offers considerations to help the U.S. Air Force strengthen how China-relevant knowledge and skills are developed, tracked, and leveraged. bit.ly/4t7V11r
Robots recently captured a Russian position in Ukraine. But don't worry about real-life terminators just yet, says RAND Europe's Jacob Parakilas. bit.ly/4u0J39Y

"Korea's energy security is no longer merely an economic issue," says RAND's Miyeon Oh.

"The time for strategic transformation is now." bit.ly/48U51Dt

What happens when schools facing similar challenges work together—rather than alone—to improve outcomes for students?

A new evaluation from RAND, @AIRInforms, and @MathematicaNow finds that networked continuous improvement can help: gates.ly/4u8UUTL via @gatesfoundation

AI is reshaping the CBRN risk landscape.

This new paper identifies urgent research questions that must be addressed to better understand the impacts: bit.ly/4vD2aZq

Millions of tons of critical minerals are thought to be sitting on the seabed, far more than miners could ever find on land.

By most estimates, those seabed nodules could more than meet U.S. demand in the decades to come. bit.ly/4dQFq1E
The capture of an enemy position by Ukrainian robots is a milestone in warfare, says @RANDEurope's Jacob Parakilas, but it shouldn't be overinterpreted. bit.ly/4cG9H10
As the U.S. Space Force shifts from start-up to mature operations, its challenge is to transform deliberately into a warfighting force purpose-built to contest and control space. bit.ly/3QbDyqE

As China emerges as America's primary pacing threat, understanding what specific knowledge and skills are required to understand, anticipate, and compete with this strategic rival will be key.

This new report outlines considerations for the U.S. Air Force: bit.ly/41vMJo8
President Trump's plan for government-sponsored retirement accounts could *save* federal and state governments trillions of dollars over time: bit.ly/416Gkzu

"People see seabed mining as … an opportunity to escape China's control of the market. But if other countries don't start to figure out how to enter this market and process these nodules, that's just another resource that China will probably dominate." bit.ly/483jpZW

South Korea sits at a geopolitical crossroads yet depends on imports for 90–95% of its energy—a structural vulnerability, says RAND's Miyeon Oh.

"The Hormuz crisis should serve as a wake-up call to prepare for potential disruptions in the Taiwan Strait." bit.ly/481V2vB

During previous periods of strategic competition, the U.S. military built its competitive advantage by cultivating deep regional expertise.

New research can help the U.S. Air Force define and determine how to build the capabilities needed to compete effectively with China. bit.ly/3Op6EC5
Here's how RAND research is helping the U.S. Space Force shift from start-up to mature operations. bit.ly/4vCu7kg

"We need to find alternative sources of these critical minerals that don't involve China. This is an all-of-government, all-hands effort. Seabed mining is one way we might accomplish it." bit.ly/4tS6diG

"The turbulence in the Taiwan Strait and the Strait of Hormuz sends a clear message: unless Korea fundamentally restructures its energy architecture, it will remain perilously exposed to external shocks." bit.ly/48yQXPG
